reason: Both identify the same root cause at the same location: the subquery condition is `status = 'failed'` when it should exclude failed runs (`status != 'failed'`). Both describe the same two runtime consequences: (1) when no run has failed, MAX(id) over an empty set returns NULL, causing latestBacklog to return nothing / the gauge to report empty backlog indefinitely; (2) when a run has failed, the subquery incorrectly keys off that failed run's id, surfacing a stale/unobserved backlog value instead of the most recent real observation, and failing to reflect a genuine clean sweep. This is a paraphrase of the same mechanism, not a different bug or vague complaint.
